author: Claude (claude-opus-5-5), logged-in subscription session; no API keys, no paid calls
scope: Google Calendar and Outlook/Microsoft 365 operational tasks not answered by the 73 baseline English pages. Excludes Codex's eight RFC/iCalendar, secondary-calendar ownership and meeting-notes topics.
evidenceMethod: Official help bodies read via WebFetch on 2026-10-23 (the fetch tool returns extracted/condensed page text, not a byte-exact copy). Claims are limited to passages returned as quotations. No first-hand UI tests, user quotations, search volumes or ranks.
mergeDecisions: Google working hours, working location, out of office and focus time were merged into one decision page instead of two thinner pages (expanded briefs 032/033 plus focus-time source).
Google 'propose a new time' was NOT claimed: keeping-track-of-who-replied already contains the Google and Apple proposal workflow.

Google sender block (brief 044) was NOT claimed: unwanted-calendar-events-iphone already answers reporting and known-sender invitation settings; a single-sender block page would be a thin near-duplicate.
Microsoft delegation briefs 056-062/067-070 were split into exactly two tasks: the owner's grant decision (delegate vs editor) and the helper's act of scheduling on the owner's behalf.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Google Calendar working location vs out of office
briefs.distinctQuestion: Which of Google's four availability signals (working hours, working location, out of office, focus time) should I set for a given situation, and which ones decline meetings?
briefs.boundary: Covers Google Workspace availability signals only. Does not cover personal/work calendar overview in Cloud Calendars, Outlook Show As (separate page), or Time Insights analysis.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Google Calendar private event who can see
briefs.distinctQuestion: When I mark one event Private, Public or Default visibility, what does each person with a given calendar permission actually see?
briefs.boundary: Event-level visibility crossed with calendar-level permission. The existing page chooses calendar-level permission; this page resolves one event's visibility and the free/busy interaction. No task-visibility depth (can-others-see-google-calendar-tasks).

briefs.primaryKeyword: Google appointment schedule check calendars for conflicts
briefs.distinctQuestion: Why does my Google booking page offer (or hide) a slot, and which calendars, responses and date exceptions control it?
briefs.boundary: Availability mechanics inside an existing Google appointment schedule. The existing page decides booking link vs invitation vs shared calendar; it does not explain conflict calendars, RSVP effects or adjusted availability. Payments, verification and cancellation remain separate candidates.

briefs.distinctQuestion: How do I hand a meeting I organise to a colleague so it keeps working (including Google Meet) after I step away?
briefs.boundary: Event organiser transfer and Meet-policy consequence. Moving an event between one's own calendars is answered by event-saved-to-wrong-calendar; transferring a whole secondary calendar is Codex's assignment and is excluded.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Google Calendar find a time not showing availability
briefs.distinctQuestion: When Find a time shows a gap for a guest, how do I tell whether they are actually free or I simply cannot see their schedule?
briefs.boundary: Organiser-side reading of Find a time. Not booking pages, not room reservation policy (calendar-event-or-room-reservation), not AI-suggested times.

briefs.distinctQuestion: Should an assistant get Can edit or Delegate on my Outlook calendar, and which extra delegate options (private items, invitation routing, categories) should I tick?
briefs.boundary: Owner's grant decision in Microsoft 365/Exchange Online. Acting on the owner's behalf is the next page; Google permissions and Cloud Calendars roles are out of scope.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Outlook send meeting on behalf of manager
briefs.distinctQuestion: As a delegate, how do I create a meeting on my manager's calendar so it is saved and sent from the right place, and what will attendees see?
briefs.boundary: Helper's procedure in Outlook on the web: Save to calendar, on-behalf identity, response routing, irreversible calendar choice, Send As escalation. Grant decision is the previous page.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Outlook share calendar can view when I'm busy
briefs.distinctQuestion: Which Outlook sharing level gives a colleague only availability, titles and locations, or full details, and what does the My organization default still reveal after I remove someone?
briefs.boundary: Inside-organization Microsoft 365 sharing levels and the new sharing model. External sharing is a separate page; Google permissions are the existing page.

briefs.primaryKeyword: share Outlook calendar with external user
briefs.distinctQuestion: Why can't I give an external partner the access I chose, and what will they actually receive when I share my Microsoft 365 calendar outside the organisation?
briefs.boundary: Tenant admin setting vs user choice vs recipient's service. Not app consent (covered in exchange-calendars-on-an-iphone), not publishing a public HTML calendar for a website.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Outlook show as working elsewhere vs out of office
briefs.distinctQuestion: Which Show As status should an Outlook appointment carry, and when should automatic replies block the calendar or decline meetings instead?
briefs.boundary: Outlook availability states and automatic-reply calendar options. Google signals are the Google page; Scheduling Assistant reading is used only to verify the result.

briefs.distinctQuestion: What happens when an attendee forwards my Outlook meeting, how do I stop it, and what can still leak?
briefs.boundary: Outlook forwarding and Allow forwarding. The existing page covers Google guest permissions (invite others, see guest list). Sending meeting information without inviting is included only as the safe alternative.

briefs.primaryKeyword: Microsoft 365 group calendar vs shared calendar
briefs.distinctQuestion: Should a team put events on a Microsoft 365 group calendar or on a shared personal calendar, given who can cancel events and who gets invited?
briefs.boundary: Microsoft 365 group calendar semantics vs owner-controlled shared calendar. Not Google Groups access (why-a-shared-calendar-does-not-appear), not Cloud Calendars sharing roles.
